description:
## Goal

Replace the current `(data, module)` pair stored per Transcript slot with a single struct, dispatched via an `OctoPi.TUI.Render` protocol. Drop the `Transcript.Entry` struct, drop the explicit `mod` arg from `Transcript.append/4`.

## Motivation

Today every Transcript entry carries two pieces of bookkeeping:

- `data` — canonical state (a binary for text/thinking blocks; a struct for everything else)
- `module` — pointer to a `Transcript.Renderer`-behaviour module, passed explicitly at `append/4` time

This was justified back when entry data could be anything (binaries, tuples, structs). After `.13` flattened the transcript and `.14` consolidated to spans, every live caller actually passes a struct. The `module` arg has become redundant — the struct already identifies the renderer kind.

Protocol dispatch on the entry struct collapses both fields into one. Drops `Entry`. Drops the explicit module arg. Replaces `function_exported?(mod, :span, 0)` reflection with a protocol callback.

## Design

### Protocol

```elixir
defprotocol OctoPi.TUI.Render do
  @fallback_to_any true

  def new(self, ctx)               # initialize state from canonical struct + ctx
  def put(self, snapshot)          # mid-stream update
  def finalize(self, snapshot)     # final state — to_lines runs once after this
  def to_lines(self)               # produce [String.t()] (no embedded \n)
  def span(self)                   # :open | :close | nil
  def wrap_span(self, lines, close_data | nil)  # only meaningful for :open
end
```

### `Any` fallback covers every existing component

Most entry kinds today (UserMessage, ToolExecution, BashExecution, CompactionSummaryMessage, Diff) already implement `OctoPi.TUI.Component` and just need their `render(self, width)` called. Instead of hand-writing six `defimpl Render` blocks, a single fallback handles all of them:

```elixir
defimpl OctoPi.TUI.Render, for: Any do
  # Bake width onto the struct if it has a :width field; otherwise no-op.
  def new(self, %{width: w}) when is_integer(w) do
    if Map.has_key?(self, :width), do: %{self | width: w}, else: self
  end
  def new(self, _), do: self

  def put(self, _),      do: self
  def finalize(self, _), do: self

  def to_lines(%mod{} = self) do
    mod.render(self, Map.get(self, :width) || 80)
  end

  def span(_),                  do: nil
  def wrap_span(_, lines, _),   do: lines
end
```

This means: **zero boilerplate for components.** Any struct that implements `Component.render/2` works out of the box. They only need a `:width` field if they care about width (most already have one). No `use` macro, no per-component `defimpl`.

### Per-kind impls only where the protocol does something non-trivial

Only the four entry kinds with real renderer logic need their own `defimpl Render`:

- `Entry.Text` — incremental markdown via `MdRender`
- `Entry.Thinking` — italic ANSI wrap
- `AssistantHeader` — `:open` span + `wrap_span/3` owns OSC bytes
- `AssistantStatus` — `:close` span

That's four `defimpl` blocks total, not ten.

### Entry structs for text/thinking

Today text/thinking blocks store the snapshot as a raw binary. Wrap each in a small struct so the protocol has something to dispatch on:

```elixir
defmodule OctoPi.TUI.Entry.Text do
  defstruct [:snapshot, :md_render]
end

defmodule OctoPi.TUI.Entry.Thinking do
  defstruct [:snapshot, :theme, :width, :hide?, :hidden_label]
end
```

The struct carries both the canonical snapshot and the intermediate renderer state. `Render.new/2` initializes the state from snapshot + ctx; `Render.put/2` advances it; `Render.finalize/2` seals it.

### Transcript

```elixir
%Transcript{
  order:     [id, ...],          # newest-head, O(1) append
  streaming: %{id => struct},    # active state
  rendered:  %{id => [String.t()]},
  ctx:       term() | nil
}

@spec append(t(), id(), struct()) :: t()
def append(%__MODULE__{} = t, id, %_{} = entry) do
  %{t | order: [id | t.order],
        streaming: Map.put(t.streaming, id, Render.new(entry, t.ctx))}
end

@spec update(t(), id(), term()) :: t()
def update(%__MODULE__{} = t, id, snapshot) do
  state = Render.put(Map.fetch!(t.streaming, id), snapshot)
  %{t | streaming: Map.put(t.streaming, id, state)}
end

@spec finalize(t(), id(), term()) :: t()
def finalize(%__MODULE__{} = t, id, snapshot) do
  state = Render.finalize(Map.fetch!(t.streaming, id), snapshot)
  %{t | streaming: Map.delete(t.streaming, id),
        rendered:  Map.put(t.rendered, id, Render.to_lines(state))}
end
```

`compose/1` dispatches `Render.span/1` and `Render.wrap_span/3` on the streaming struct (or, for finalized entries, on a snapshot we keep around for span lookup — see open question).

`Entry` struct deleted. `entries` map deleted. `fetch_module!/2` deleted.

### Open question: snapshot lookup after finalize

`Interactive.maybe_update_header_tool_flag` reads `Transcript.fetch_data!` *after* the header is finalized but before the status arrives. With Entry dropped, finalized entries no longer have their canonical struct retained anywhere — only `[String.t()]` lines in `rendered`.

Options:

1. **Keep a tiny `data: %{id => struct}` map** alongside `streaming`. Cheap. Preserves `fetch_data!`/`get_data` semantics. Costs one extra map lookup on finalize.
2. **Forbid post-finalize data lookup.** Forces `maybe_update_header_tool_flag` to update the header *before* finalize (which is what it does today, but the call site reads back after). One callsite to refactor.
3. **Stash entry struct on the streaming map even after finalize** with a tombstone marker. Conflates streaming/finalized; bad.

Recommended: (1). Keep `data: %{}` for finalized lookups. Tiny.

## Migration plan

1. **Define `OctoPi.TUI.Render` protocol** with the six callbacks and the `Any` fallback.
2. **Migrate the four span-aware structs** — `AssistantHeader`, `AssistantStatus`, `Entry.Text`, `Entry.Thinking`. Each gets one `defimpl Render`. Existing logic carries over from the current `Transcript.Renderer` behaviour impls.
3. **Components: nothing.** UserMessage, ToolExecution, BashExecution, CompactionSummaryMessage, Diff all work via the `Any` fallback. Add `:width` field to any struct that doesn't have one and needs it.
4. **Rewrite `Transcript`.** Drop `Entry`, drop the `entries` map, change `append/4` to `append/3`. Compose dispatches via protocol.
5. **Update `Interactive`** callsites:
   - `Transcript.append(t, k, snap, TextBlock)` → `Transcript.append(t, k, %Entry.Text{snapshot: snap})`
   - same for thinking, header, status, csm, bash, tool, user — drop the trailing module arg, wrap binaries in entry structs.
6. **Update `AssistantMessage` component.** It builds a nested Transcript for blocks; same migration.
7. **Tests.** Mechanical rename + struct wrapping.

## Acceptance

- `mix test` green (1286 / 0).
- `mix credo --strict` clean on all touched files.
- `mix format --check-formatted` clean.
- `mix dialyzer` no new warnings (current baseline: 3 pre-existing).
- `Transcript.Entry` module deleted. `Transcript.append/4` is now `Transcript.append/3` taking `(t, id, struct)`.
- No `function_exported?` calls in `Transcript`.
- Component structs (UserMessage, Diff, etc.) gain at most a `:width` field; no per-component `defimpl Render` needed.
- Visual smoke test in tmux: streaming render unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Any change to OSC injection semantics (already correct from `.14`).
- Performance work beyond what falls out of the simplification.
- Persisting transcripts (the data/state merger makes serialization slightly weirder; address if/when needed).
title: Render protocol: drop Entry, dispatch on entry struct
